clue.text: Pub on map is keeping to route

indicators.note: a pub sign keeping something holds it inside, so the other letters go within

parts.note: PH is the abbreviation for a public house on Ordnance Survey maps
to and at both mark a place you arrive at, as in 'at the door'

explanation.surface: Directions read off a map: the walker heads for the pub marked on it.
explanation.walkthrough: British Ordnance Survey maps mark a public house with two letters; 'is keeping' holds the piece for 'to' inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A path is a way or course along which one travels, a synonym for a route.

clue.text: Papers, sticking together, adopt sabre rattling

indicators.note: rattling shakes things about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Newspapers that stick together take up sabre-rattling rhetoric.
explanation.definitionFit: Board made by gluing sheets of paper together is stiff card of layered sheets.

clue.text: A little less than honest politician

definitions.text: A little less than honest politician

indicators.note: a little less means a small piece, the last letter, is lost

parts.note: true means honest
MP, member of parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A jibe at a politician who is not quite honest.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a dig at the US president of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue paints a well-known American president as a politician short of honesty.

clue.text: Old hard form of silica surrounds geographical feature

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: the rearranged silica letters are placed around the other piece
a new form of the word silica means its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A geology note: an old, hard form of silica encloses some landscape feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges the word silica into ISICAL; 'surrounds' wraps it round the craggy hill, a word used in southwest England.
explanation.definitionFit: Something historical belongs to or concerns the past, so it is old in sense.

clue.text: This month old NI police need time to train

parts.note: inst., instant, is the old business abbreviation for this month
the RUC, Royal Ulster Constabulary, was Northern Ireland's police force until 2001

explanation.surface: Former Northern Ireland police officers need time this month to train.
explanation.definitionFit: To instruct is to teach or coach someone in a skill.

clue.text: Least scary exam takes a minute

indicators.note: takes means the exam holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a test is an exam

explanation.surface: The least frightening exam is one that lasts only a minute.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals that are most docile or domesticated are the least frightening.

clue.text: Regularly come round about a dog

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A dog regularly comes round the house.
explanation.definitionFit: To happen repeatedly is to come round again and again.

clue.text: Kill off 'Terminator'? — it's full of holes

parts.note: to cull is to kill off selected animals
an ender is something that terminates

explanation.surface: A film fan asks whether the Terminator kills off, and finds the plot full of holes.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a variant spelling of colander, the kitchen strainer.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen strainer for draining vegetables is perforated all over.

clue.text: Light area

definitions.meaning: to light means to alight, come down onto a surface

explanation.surface: An illuminated region.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird lights on a branch, coming down to rest; a country or territory is a region.

clue.text: Imagine another time when ruined terrace's laid over earth

indicators.note: in a down answer, laid over puts the rearranged terrace on top
ruined says the letters of the word terrace are wrecked and rearranged

parts.note: the word terrace, with the 's read as 'has', supplies the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A ruined terrace has been buried under earth, and one imagines how it was.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of terrace's is read as 'has', and the anagram uses only TERRACE.
explanation.definitionFit: To recreate is to make or picture something anew, imagining it once more.

clue.text: Mouth is where some say river begins

indicators.note: some speakers, without a sounded R, pronounce one word like the other

parts.note: a river begins at its source, the spring it rises from

explanation.surface: A geography quibble: the mouth is where some claim a river starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouth' looks like a river's mouth but means cheek or insolence; in non-rhotic British speech SOURCE and SAUCE sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Mouth and sauce are both informal words for impudent talk or cheek.

clue.text: What's this?; a house, almost a settlement

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house

indicators.note: almost means the final letter of the settlement word is dropped

parts.note: a colony is a settlement of people in a new land

explanation.surface: Someone asks about a house and an almost-settlement, with an odd punctuation mark.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the punctuation mark printed in the clue itself; SEMI is the British term for a semi-detached house.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed mark ; after the question mark is the punctuation sign called by this name.

clue.text: He rules fifth-rate politician's a gutless mistake

parts.note: E is the fifth grade after A to D
MP, member of parliament, is a politician

indicators.note: gutless means losing the innards, here one middle letter

parts.note: an error is a mistake

explanation.surface: A ruler is dismissed as a lowly politician whose career is a feeble blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutless' removes the central R of ERROR to leave EROR.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is a sovereign ruler of an empire, someone who reigns.

clue.text: Nechayev, Russian revolutionary, conceals this plot for 31

indicators.note: revolutionary says the hidden letters are read backwards
conceals says the letters sit hidden within the named words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The Russian revolutionary Nechayev hides a plot, as conspirators do.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'conceals this plot for' as definition; 'conceals' is the hiding signal and 'this' a link, so the definition is 'plot for 31', referring to the plans of 31 across.
explanation.definitionFit: To survey land is to measure and plot it so charts can be drawn from it.

clue.text: Burns before composing ode errs, caught with proctor's jacket

indicators.note: a jacket is the outer layer, so the first and last letters of proctor
composing arranges the letters of ode errs in new order

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A poet burns his ode before a university proctor catches its errors.
explanation.definitionFit: To burn a disc is to record onto it, so burns ahead of time means records in advance.

clue.text: We see no dancer waving arms

indicators.note: waving moves things about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An observer notes there is no dancer waving her arms about.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordnance is military weaponry, especially artillery, so it means weapons collectively.

clue.text: Use garden rocks and overalls

indicators.note: rocks shakes something up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: use garden rocks and wear overalls.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungarees are trousers with a bib and straps, a kind of work overall.

clue.text: 30 of more high quality diamonds within

indicators.note: within places the suit letter inside the other piece

parts.note: finer means of higher quality
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A jeweller compares stones: higher quality with diamonds set inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who first spots a thing is its discoverer, the same idea as one who locates it.

clue.text: One will cut down oak, say, upset thanks to abuse

parts.note: I'll is the contraction of I will, one saying they will

indicators.note: cut down means the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: an oak is an example of a tree

indicators.note: upset turns the word over, so in a down answer it reads upwards

parts.note: ta is British informal thanks

explanation.surface: Someone vows to fell an oak, upsetting those who abuse thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut down' fits a tree but here trims its last letter, leaving TRE; 'upset' turns TA into AT.
explanation.definitionFit: To ill-treat is to mistreat or harm someone, the same as abusing them.

clue.text: Heading off for gender reassignment and a short conversation

indicators.note: heading off removes the first letter

parts.note: a sex change is gender reassignment

explanation.surface: Someone sets off for gender reassignment after a brief chat.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief back-and-forth of words between people is an exchange of views.

clue.text: Senior Guide's bit of road rage

indicators.note: a bit of the word road is its first letter

parts.note: rage is anger

explanation.surface: A senior Girl Guide gets a taste of road rage.
explanation.walkthrough: In British Guiding, a Ranger is a member of the senior section, older than ordinary Guides.
explanation.definitionFit: The older girls' section of the Guide movement has members named for forest wardens.

clue.text: He searches place with gold in meet of rivers

indicators.note: in puts place and gold inside the meeting of rivers

parts.note: the rivers are the Exe, in Devon, and R, the map abbreviation for river, placed together
PL is the abbreviation for place in street names
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A prospector searches for a gold spot where two rivers join.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in Devon, southwest England.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who travels into unknown regions to investigate is a searcher.

clue.text: Busy disc jockey on ecstasy leaves part of speech

indicators.note: leaves means the letters depart from the longer word

parts.note: an adjective is a part of speech
DJ is the abbreviation for disc jockey
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A busy disc jockey on ecstasy walks out mid-sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: The D, J and E removed are scattered in ADJECTIVE, not one run.
explanation.definitionFit: Being busy means being occupied and energetically engaged, i.e. lively and on the go.

clue.text: Chap with current account? He's lost it

parts.note: a chap is a man
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A man with a bank current account who has lost his money, or his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current account' looks like one banking term but splits into current (I) and account (AC).
explanation.definitionFit: A madman has lost his mind: 'lost it' is the idiom for going crazy.

clue.text: I am adult fly perhaps

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
A is the film classification for adult
to fly is to go

explanation.surface: An insect announces it has reached adulthood.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay; 'perhaps' marks the fly as one example of an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The final, sexually mature stage of an insect after metamorphosis is the imago.

clue.text: Dissident in this place has mark of approval curtailed

parts.note: here means in this place

indicators.note: curtailed means the tail, the last letter, is cut off

parts.note: a tick is a mark of approval on work

explanation.surface: A dissident on the spot has his approval mark cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissenter from accepted doctrine is someone who holds unorthodox beliefs.

clue.text: When climbing cracking section in a bone

indicators.note: climbing in a down answer means the letters read upwards

parts.note: A1, written AI, means first-rate or cracking
a bit is a section or piece

explanation.surface: A climber cracks a section of a bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The shinbone in the lower leg is the larger of its two bones.

clue.text: Soldiers put up notice in thoroughfare

indicators.note: put up in a down answer means the letters are raised to read upwards

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: Soldiers put up a notice on a street.
explanation.definitionFit: A public street or highway along which traffic passes is a thoroughfare.

clue.text: Running exercises featured in speech

indicators.note: featured in says the exercises appear inside the speech

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: A speech mentions running as one of the exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: Running a business is its management or functioning, as in a firm in full working.

clue.text: Casual walker taking left gets to a traffic light

indicators.note: taking away the letter for left removes it

parts.note: an ambler is someone strolling casually

explanation.surface: A stroller turns left and arrives at a set of traffic lights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' looks like adding, but here it means taking away the L.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow-orange signal between red and green on a traffic signal has this colour name.

clue.text: The first to spot a saucer perhaps above outskirts of Exeter?

parts.note: a saucer is one example of a disc shape
over means above

indicators.note: the outskirts of the word Exeter are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone first spots a flying saucer hovering over the edge of Exeter.
explanation.walkthrough: Exeter is a city in Devon, southwest England.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who finds something before anyone else is credited as its finder.

clue.text: Plans on having junk mail sent back

indicators.note: sent back means the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: spam is unwanted junk email

explanation.surface: Someone's plans include returning unwanted junk mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Charts of an area are drawings or plans of it.
